info.title: Sandesh
info.description: Local mail infrastructure for developers. REST over the mail core; the WebSocket event stream at `/api/v1/events` is documented in `docs/EVENT_MODEL.md`, because OpenAPI cannot describe a WebSocket protocol.

get.description:
The retrieval half of Phase 7 A2. Transcripts have been captured and stored
since ADR-066 with no way to read them back, so the phase's criterion —
"every connection to every protocol produces a **retrievable** trace" — was
met on the capture side and unmet end to end.

`?protocol=smtp|imap|pop3` filters; omitting it returns every protocol
interleaved, which is what "what just happened?" usually means.

# Errors
`400` if `limit` or `protocol` is unusable, `503` when tracing is disabled.

parameters.description: Filter by smtp, imap or pop3

get.description:
# Errors
`400` for a malformed id, `404` if no such record, `503` when tracing is
disabled.

The counterpart to `/messages/{id}/delivery`, and not merely a convenience:
a transaction rejected outright stores no message, so its record has no
message id to look it up by and is reachable *only* here. Without this
endpoint the rejection records would be written and then invisible, which
is worse than not writing them.

# Errors
`400` if `limit` is out of range.

get.description:
Always answerable: no fault configured is `active: false` with an empty
list, which is a true reading rather than a missing capability. That is why
this has no `503` the way the trace endpoints do (ADR-077).

post.description:
Adds rather than replaces, so a scenario can build up several rules without
re-sending the ones already set. `DELETE` is the way to start over, which
keeps "add one" and "replace all" from being the same call with different
bodies.

delete.description:
Returns the resulting (empty) state rather than `204`, so a caller that
clears and then asserts needs one request instead of two.

get.description:
Touches no dependency. If the process can route a request it is alive, and
making liveness query the database turns a slow disk into a restart loop.

Unlike liveness this does check the database, and answers `503` when it is
unreachable. Reporting ready while storage is down would be a lie that costs
a caller a confusing failure later.

post.description:
Bulk import of an `mboxrd` file or a single `.eml`. Each framed message goes
through the same placement path as an injection, so an imported message is
indistinguishable from one that arrived over SMTP.

# Errors
`400` for an unknown format, an empty body, or a payload that frames into
no messages.

parameters.name: mailbox_id
parameters.description: Optional target mailbox ID to place all imported messages directly into.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/logs/stream` — the live log, as Server-Sent Events.
get.description:
SSE rather than a `WebSocket`: the stream is one-directional, so the
client never needs to send anything, and this mirrors the existing
`/events/sse` mirror rather than inventing a second `WebSocket` surface.

A lagging consumer is skipped past rather than disconnected. Dropping the
oldest lines matches the event bus's stance (`sandesh-events`): a reader
this far behind wants what is happening now, and the backlog endpoint is
there for anyone who needs to catch up.

get.description:
The interpreted view of the same headers `/headers` returns flat: the
`Received:` chain as a chronological hop list with per-hop delay, and the
authentication headers upstream left behind.

**Nothing here is verified.** The response carries a `disclaimer` field
stating so, because a client that renders `dkim=pass` without the caveat
would be claiming something Sandesh has not checked.

# Errors
`400` for an unparseable id, `404` if no such message exists.

Every URL the message's HTML parts reference, classified by the role the
markup gives it, with the distinct hosts summarised.

**No URL here is fetched.** Extraction is entirely local (ADR-090):
a mail server that resolved the links in mail it received would be an
SSRF vector pointed at whatever a message chose, and would confirm to a
sender that their message was opened. The response carries a `disclaimer`
field saying so, for the same reason the header analysis does.

A message with no HTML part returns an empty report, not a `404` — "this
message references nothing" is an answer.

# Errors
`400` for an unparseable id, `404` if no such message exists.

200.description: Extracted — not resolved — links and images

get.description:
Parts are reported as byte ranges into the raw message, which is how they
are stored (`CORE_SPEC.md`). There is no second MIME representation here —
the API projects the one the core already has.

`400` for an unparseable id, `404` if no such message exists.

200.description: The MIME tree with raw byte ranges

get.description:
Returns the decoded body (transfer encodings such as Base64 and Quoted-Printable
decoded). Set `?raw=true` to retrieve the verbatim encoded bytes as stored.

`400` for an unparseable id or part path, `404` if no such message or part exists.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Dotted MIME part path; `root` for the top part

parameters.name: raw
parameters.description:
Return the raw, undecoded bytes as stored in the message, instead of the
decoded content. Defaults to `false`.

get.description:
One of Sandesh's core correctness guarantees. The bytes are written to the
body untouched: no UTF-8 conversion, no line-ending normalisation, no
re-encoding. What SMTP received is what comes back.

# Errors
`400` for an unparseable id, `404` if no such message exists.

post.description:
Re-delivers a stored message through the same placement path a fresh
injection uses, with a new `Message-ID` and a recorded link back to the
source (`X-Sandesh-Replay-Of` in the bytes, `replay_of` on the delivery).

# Errors
`400` for an unparseable id, `404` if no such message exists.

201.description: The message was replayed as a new message

# Errors

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/rules` — the configured rules, in evaluation order.
# Errors
[`ApiError`] if the rules could not be read.

post.description:
The keyword is validated here, not at delivery time. An invalid one would
otherwise be stored, fail to decode on every read, and silently never fire —
a rule that exists in the list and does nothing, which is worse than a `400`.

An empty condition list is refused for the same reason it matches nothing in
the domain: a rule that tags every message is never what a half-finished
configuration meant, and refusing it here is the only place it can be said
out loud.
# Errors
[`ApiError`] if the keyword is invalid, no conditions were given, or the
rule could not be stored.

delete.description:
Deliveries that already recorded it keep their record: the match stored the
rule's name rather than a reference, so removing a rule cannot erase the
explanation of what it did while it existed (ADR-087).
# Errors
[`ApiError`] if the id is malformed or names no configured rule.

get.description:
Searches messages using developer filter syntax (`from:`, `to:`, `subject:`,
`is:unread`, `has:attachment`, `larger:`, `smaller:` and free text terms).

200.description: A page of matching message summaries

get.description: Explains how a search filter string is compiled into the domain query plan.

post.description:
Accepts a structured message request, synthesizes an RFC 5322 MIME message,
resolves recipients to their respective `INBOX` mailboxes, places a copy
into the sender's `Sent` mailbox, and persists the message through
[`MessageStore`].

# Errors
`400` if recipient list is empty or from address is missing.

get.description:
Always answerable, like `/faults`: no endpoint registered is an empty list,
which is a true reading rather than a missing capability.
# Errors
[`ApiError`] if the endpoints could not be read.

post.description:
The URL is validated here rather than at send time. An endpoint that cannot
be parsed would otherwise be accepted, enqueue notifications for every
delivery, and fail all of them — turning a typo into a backlog of terminal
failures instead of a `400`.
# Errors
[`ApiError`] if the URL is not absolute, or the endpoint could not be stored.

201.description: The endpoint was registered; the only response carrying `secret`

get.description:
Includes delivered and terminally-failed entries, not only what is
outstanding: the question this view answers is "did my webhook fire?", and
a list of only pending work cannot answer it.
# Errors
[`ApiError`] if the outbox could not be read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Defaults and caps as elsewhere.

delete.description:
The cascade is deliberate: a pending notification for a destination that no
longer exists is undeliverable, and letting it retry its way to terminal
failure would fill the outbox view with noise about a decision already made.
# Errors
[`ApiError`] if the id is malformed or names no registered endpoint.

addresses.description: The addresses that route to it.

has_password.description: Whether this account has a configured password.

is_catch_all.description: Whether it receives mail for unmatched recipients.

AddressDto.description: An email address as the API renders it.

display_name.description: The display name, when the header carried one.

is_inline.description: Whether it is `inline` rather than an attachment proper.

AuthResultDto.description:
One method's entry from an `Authentication-Results:` field.

`result` is the upstream server's word, reproduced. Sandesh did not check it.

authserv_id.description: The host claiming to have performed the check.

result.description: The result as written upstream, e.g. `pass`. Not checked here.

oneOf.description: Mark all specified entries as seen (`\Seen`).
Mark all specified entries as unseen (remove `\Seen`).
Move all specified entries to target mailbox.

move.description: Move all specified entries to target mailbox.

BulkAction.description: Action to perform across multiple entries (`POST /api/v1/entries/bulk`).

BulkEntriesRequest.description: Request body for bulk operations on entries (`POST /api/v1/entries/bulk`).

BulkEntriesResponse.description: Response returned from a bulk operation.

ConnectionDto.description:
One connection's protocol transcript (`GET /api/v1/connections/{id}`).

The retrieval half of ADR-066: the capture side has been storing these since
A2's first half, with no way to read them back, so the Phase 7 criterion
"every connection produces a **retrievable** trace" was only half met.

The transcript is already redacted at capture time — credentials never reach
storage, and message bodies become a byte count (ADR-066) — so this DTO does
no filtering of its own. Redacting here instead would put the guarantee on
the read path, where a second reader (a future export, a log stream) would
not inherit it.

closed_at.description: When it closed, RFC 3339. `null` while still open.

disposition.description:
How it ended: `closed`, `disconnected`, `server_closed` or
`shutting_down`. `null` while still open.

duration_us.description: How long it lasted, in microseconds. `null` while still open.

encrypted.description:
Whether the transport was encrypted **when the connection closed**.

A `STARTTLS` connection is one record that begins in cleartext and ends
encrypted, so this is the final state. The transcript shows where the
upgrade happened.

opened_at.description: When the socket was accepted, RFC 3339.

peer.description: The client address, when the transport had one.

protocol.description: Which protocol server accepted it: `smtp`, `imap` or `pop3`.

transcript.description:
The transcript, one entry per line.

Always present, including in the list response. A transcript is the
whole point of the record and is already capped at capture time, so
omitting it from the list would mean a second round trip per row to see
the only field anyone opened the view for.

truncated.description:
Whether the transcript hit its cap and was cut short.

Reported so a reader can tell a quiet connection from a truncated one —
without it, a trace that stops mid-session looks like a client that went
silent.

CopyEntryRequest.description: Request body for copying an entry to another mailbox (`POST /api/v1/entries/{id}/copy`).

CreateAccountRequest.description: Request body for creating an account (`POST /api/v1/accounts`).

addresses.description: Optional addresses routing to this account.

is_catch_all.description: Whether this is the catch-all account.

CreateMailboxRequest.description: Request body for creating a mailbox (`POST /api/v1/mailboxes`).

account_id.description: Optional account UUID. Defaults to the catch-all or primary account if omitted.

CreateWorkspaceRequest.description: Request payload to create a new workspace.

auth_required.description: Whether to require authentication for SMTP/IMAP/POP3 in this workspace.

clone_from.description: Optional source workspace identifier to clone accounts and routing rules from.

id.description: Optional slug identifier. If omitted, generated from name.

oneOf.description: Optional initial account setup when not cloning from an existing workspace.

password.description: Optional password for initial account authentication.

set_active.description: Whether to immediately switch to this workspace upon creation.

allOf.description: The endpoint as it will read from now on.

secret.description:
The signing secret, in clear, for the only time.

`None` when the endpoint is unsigned. Store it now: it cannot be
recovered, only replaced by registering the endpoint again.

CreatedWebhookDto.description:
The response to registering an endpoint (`POST /api/v1/webhooks`).

Distinct from [`WebhookEndpointDto`] for one reason: it carries `secret`,
and this is the only response that ever will. Giving the read type an
optional field that is populated exactly once would make every consumer
handle a value they cannot otherwise obtain, and would put the key one
forgotten `null` check away from a listing.

DeliveryDto.description:
How a message reached Sandesh (`GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/delivery`).

Envelope recipients live here rather than on the message because they are a
property of the *delivery*, not of the immutable bytes (ADR-019). This is
what makes `Bcc` visible: a recipient that appears in no header still
appears here.

duration_us.description: How long the transaction took, in microseconds.

helo.description:
The domain the client gave in `EHLO`/`HELO`. Unverified, as SMTP makes
it unverifiable: it is what the client claimed, not what it is.

message_id.description: The message it produced, when one was stored.

peer.description: The client address, when the ingress had one.

rcpt_to.description: SMTP `RCPT TO`, every recipient the envelope carried.

received_at.description: When the delivery was received, RFC 3339.

replay_of.description:
The message this one was replayed from, when it was a replay (A5).

The queryable half of replay provenance. The same link is written into
the replayed message as an `X-Sandesh-Replay-Of` header, which travels
with the bytes; this field is what a consumer filters on. `null` for
every ordinary delivery.

rules_applied.description:
The rules that fired, and what each added (ADR-087).

The A3 criterion is that rules are visible in the delivery record; this
is where the Delivery tab reads them from.

signed_headers.description: `h=` — the signed header names, in the order signed.

tags.description: Every tag as written, including ones not named above.

EntryDto.description: An entry addressed in its own right (`API_DESIGN.md` §3.3).

EntryRef.description: One placement of a message, as it appears inside a message summary.

mailbox_name.description: That mailbox's name, so a list view needs no second request.

ExtractedLinkDto.description: One URL found in an HTML part.

alt.description: The `alt` attribute, for images that declare one.

attribute.description: The lowercased attribute that carried it, e.g. `href`, `src`.

element.description: The lowercased element that carried it, e.g. `a`, `img`.

embedded.description:
Whether the content is carried by the message itself (`cid:`, `data:`)
rather than fetched.

host.description: The lowercased host, when the URL has an authority component.

insecure.description: Whether loading it would use plain `http:`.

part_path.description: The dotted path of the HTML part this URL came from.

scheme.description: The lowercased scheme, when the URL has one.

text.description: Visible link text, for anchors with any.

url.description:
The URL as the message wrote it, with HTML entities decoded. Not
normalised or resolved against a base.

FaultMatchDto.description:
Which conversations a fault applies to (ADR-084).

Every field absent means every conversation, which is the common case for a
CI scenario and needs no ceremony to express.

oneOf.description: Accept the recipients, then refuse the message (`554`).
Refuse temporarily (`451`), so a client retries.

delay_ms.description: How long to wait, in milliseconds.

oneOf.description: Close the connection with no reply.

FaultModeDto.description:
What an injected fault does (ADR-084).

A tagged representation rather than a flat string plus optional fields: the
delay belongs to `slow_response` and to no other mode, and a shape that
allowed `{"mode": "connection_drop", "delay_ms": 500}` would have to either
reject it or silently ignore the delay. This makes it unconstructable.

active.description:
Whether any fault is currently configured.

Redundant against `rules` being non-empty, and deliberately so: it is
what `/info` and the UI indicator read, and a single boolean is harder
to misinterpret than an array's length.

rules.description: Every configured rule, in the order they are evaluated.

HeaderAnalysisDto.description:
The analysis of one message's headers (`ROADMAP.md` Phase 7 A3).

**Parsed, never verified.** Every authentication field here is reproduced as
the upstream server wrote it. Sandesh performs no DKIM, SPF or DMARC
verification and this response makes no claim about validity — see
[`HeaderAnalysisDto::disclaimer`], which is part of the payload precisely so
that a client cannot render these fields without the caveat travelling with
them.

disclaimer.description: A fixed statement that nothing here was verified.

HeaderDto.description:
One header, raw and decoded (`API_DESIGN.md` §3.1).

Duplicates are preserved and order is the order they appeared in: a tool for
debugging mail must show what actually arrived, not a tidied map.

name.description: The field name as it appeared.

raw_value.description:
The undecoded bytes, lossily rendered for JSON transport. The raw
endpoint remains the authority for exact octets.

status.description: Always `ok` if the process can answer at all.

imported.description: How many were stored and placed.

message_ids.description: The ids of the stored messages, in payload order.

parsed.description: How many messages the payload was framed into.

InfoDto.description:
Server and connection information (`GET /api/v1/info`).

The connection strings are real product surface: they are what a developer
copies into their application's configuration.

api_auth.description:
The **API** authentication posture: `disabled` or `required`.

Separate from `smtp_auth`, which never governed the HTTP surface. Before
this existed, a deployment with `smtp_auth: required` looked protected
while the API served every message to anyone who asked (ADR-075).

api_tls.description: Whether the API is served over HTTPS.

faults_active.description:
Whether any SMTP fault is currently injected (ADR-084).

Read live from the registry on every request rather than from the
startup `ServerInfo`, because unlike every other field here it can
change while the server runs — that being the entire point of faults
being runtime state. Surfaced so an injected failure is never invisible
to someone wondering why delivery stopped working.

http_address.description: Where the HTTP listener is bound.

imap_address.description: Where the IMAP listener is bound, if it is running.

pop3_address.description: Where the POP3 listener is bound, if it is running.

smtp_address.description: Where the SMTP listener is bound, if it is running.

smtp_auth.description:
The SMTP authentication posture: `disabled`, `optional` or `required`.

Reported so the UI can state it plainly. A developer must never be
unsure whether their local mail server is accepting anonymous mail
(`UI_UX_DIRECTION` §5) — and the honest answer by default is that it is.

tls_fingerprint.description:
The certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint, when TLS is enabled.

The only way to trust a self-signed certificate deliberately rather
than by clicking through a warning is to compare this against what the
client reports.

InitialAccountSetupDto.description: Initial account configuration when creating a new workspace from scratch.

addresses.description: Bound email addresses to associate with this account.

is_catch_all.description: Whether this account receives all unmatched incoming recipient addresses.

LinkReportDto.description:
The links and images one message's HTML parts reference.

**Nothing here was fetched.** Sandesh enumerates the URLs a message
contains and never resolves them — see [`LinkReportDto::disclaimer`], which
is part of the payload so a client cannot render the list as if the
destinations had been checked.

disclaimer.description: A fixed statement that no URL here was resolved.

hosts.description: Distinct hosts referenced, lowercased and sorted.

image_count.description: Count of images the client would load.

links.description:
Every URL found, in document order, parts in tree order. Duplicates are
preserved.

resource_count.description: Count of other referenced resources (scripts, stylesheets, frames).

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` at the end.

total_estimate.description: An estimate of the total; see [`ListResponse::total_estimate`].

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` at the end.

total_estimate.description: An estimate of the total; see [`ListResponse::total_estimate`].

ListResponseConnectionDto.description: A page of connection transcripts, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` at the end.

total_estimate.description: An estimate of the total; see [`ListResponse::total_estimate`].

ListResponseDeliveryDto.description: A page of delivery records, newest first.

LogLineDto.description:
One captured log line (Phase 7 A6).

The log carries no message content by construction: bodies, headers and
credentials never reach a log line in the first place (`logging.rs`), so
this DTO — like [`ConnectionDto`] — does no filtering of its own. Putting
redaction on the read path would place the guarantee where a second reader
could not inherit it.

seq.description: Monotonic identity, so a reader can tell a gap from a quiet period.

uid_next.description: The next UID to be assigned.

allOf.description: The list-row fields, flattened in so a client has one shape to learn.

attachments.description: Attachment metadata; bytes come from the attachment endpoint.

diagnostics.description: Where parsing struggled. Non-empty is normal and interesting.

headers.description: Every header, in order, duplicates preserved.

MessageDetail.description: A message with everything the detail view needs.

MessageSummary.description:
A message as it appears in a list (`API_DESIGN.md` §4).

Deliberately excludes bodies and MIME structure. A list of 500 messages must
not carry 500 message bodies; the detail endpoint exists for that.

oneOf.description:
The `From:` header, decoded — what the sending application wrote,
display name included.

Falls back to the envelope sender (SMTP `MAIL FROM`) only when the
message has no `From:` mailbox. The envelope is usually a bounce
address with no name, so preferring it would list most application mail
under an address its author never typed; it remains available from
`GET /messages/{id}/delivery`.

has_attachments.description: Whether the message has any attachment part.

to.description:
The `To:` header, decoded.

Deliberately the header, not the envelope recipients: envelope
recipients are a property of a *delivery*, not of the immutable message
— one message delivered to three addresses has one set of bytes and
three envelope recipients. They are reported by
`GET /messages/{id}/delivery`, and the placements in `entries` show
where the message actually landed, which is what makes `Bcc` visible.

MimePartDto.description:
One node of the MIME tree (`API_DESIGN.md` §3.1).

Offsets are ranges **into the raw bytes**, matching the storage model
(`CORE_SPEC.md`): there is no second copy of the MIME content anywhere, and
a client can correlate any part with the raw endpoint exactly.

body_length.description: Length of the part body in raw bytes.

body_offset.description: Byte offset of the part body within the raw message.

is_attachment.description: Whether this part is an attachment.

path.description: Dotted part path, `""` for the root.

url_path.description:
How to address this part in a URL.

The same as `path` except for the root, whose domain rendering is the
empty string and which is therefore spelled `root` in a URL.

MimeTree.description: The MIME structure of a message.

parts.description: Every part, flattened; `children` reconstructs the tree.

MoveEntryRequest.description: Request body for moving an entry to another mailbox (`POST /api/v1/entries/{id}/move`).

NewRuleDto.description: A request to create a rule (`POST /api/v1/rules`).

add_keyword.description: The keyword to add. Must be a valid IMAP keyword.

conditions.description:
Every condition must hold. An empty list matches nothing, not
everything — a half-configured rule must not tag all mail.

enabled.description: Whether to start enabled. Defaults to true.

name.description: A human name, shown wherever the rule is reported.

NewWebhookDto.description: A request to register an endpoint (`POST /api/v1/webhooks`).

enabled.description:
Whether to start enabled. Defaults to true — registering an endpoint
that receives nothing is not what anyone means by registering one.

secret.description:
Use this secret instead of a generated one.

For pointing Sandesh at a receiver that already knows a key. Ignored
unless `sign` is set, so a secret cannot be configured on an endpoint
that will never use it.

sign.description:
Turn on payload signing.

Sandesh generates the secret and returns it once. Omitted or false
leaves the endpoint unsigned, which stays the default: a webhook
pointed at a local test receiver has nothing to spoof, and requiring a
key there would add a step to the case Sandesh exists to serve.

attempts.description: How many attempts have been made.

endpoint_id.description: Which endpoint it is bound for.

last_error.description:
Why the most recent attempt failed, if one did.

The reason a terminally-failed entry is kept rather than deleted: a
webhook that silently stopped is the opacity Phase 7 exists to remove.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt becomes due, RFC 3339.

payload.description: The JSON body, as rendered at enqueue time.

PatchAccountRequest.description: Request body for updating an account (`PATCH /api/v1/accounts/{id}`).

add_addresses.description: Additional addresses to route to this account.

remove_addresses.description: Addresses to remove from this account.

PatchMailboxRequest.description: Request body for updating a mailbox (`PATCH /api/v1/mailboxes/{id}`).

ProblemDetails.title: ProblemDetails
ProblemDetails.description:
The RFC 9457 body.

Public because it is the error half of the API contract: every non-2xx
response has this shape, so it must appear in the `OpenAPI` document and in
the generated TypeScript. Clients branch on `type`, whose slug is stable;
`title` is prose and may be reworded.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body as RFC 9457 specifies.

type.description: A URI identifying the error class.

PurgeResultDto.description: Summary returned after a purge operation completes.

purged_at.description: Purge timestamp formatted as RFC 3339 UTC.

PurgeWorkspaceRequest.description: Options for purging data in a workspace.

clear_traces.description: Whether to clear protocol connection traces.

clear_webhooks.description: Whether to clear webhook outbox logs.

database.description: Whether the database answered a trivial query.

delay_micros.description:
Microseconds since the previous hop. May be negative when relay clocks
disagree; that is reported rather than hidden.

for_recipient.description: The `for` clause: the envelope recipient this hop saw.

index.description: Zero-based position in chronological order; hop 0 is the oldest.

raw.description: The whole field value, for when the parse missed something.

timestamp.description: The hop timestamp, RFC 3339 UTC, when it parsed.

RecipientOutcomeDto.description: One recipient's outcome within a delivery.

entry_id.description:
The placement this recipient produced, when one was made. Lets the view
link a recipient to the entry it created rather than re-deriving it.

outcome.description: The domain's own stable outcome name, never `Debug` output.

reason.description: Why, when the outcome was not a plain success.

resolved_account_id.description:
The account this address resolved to, when it resolved to one. `null`
for a rejected recipient, and for a catch-all placement the id is the
catch-all account rather than one matching the address.

oneOf.description: A named header contains this text, case-insensitively.

value.description: Substring to find in the decoded value.

oneOf.description: The envelope sender contains this text.
Any envelope recipient contains this text.

RuleConditionDto.description:
One condition of a rule.

Flattened into a `kind`-tagged object, matching how `FaultModeDto` carries
its variants, so the wire form reads as one object rather than a wrapper
around a single-key map.

add_keyword.description: The keyword added to each placement when it does.

conditions.description: Every condition must hold for the rule to apply.

name.description: The name shown in the delivery record when this rule fires.

RuleMatchDto.description:
One rule firing, as reported on a delivery.

Carries the rule's name as it stood when it fired, not a live lookup: a rule
edited or deleted afterwards must not rewrite history (ADR-087).

plan.description: Debug representation of the compiled `SearchQuery` domain plan.

query.description: The user query string as received.

SendMessageRequest.description: Request body for composing and sending an email (`POST /api/v1/send`).

is_draft.description: Whether this message should be saved as a draft in Drafts instead of delivered.

SendMessageResponse.description: Response returned after successfully composing and delivering an email.

id.description: The generated UUID of the new message.

placements.description: Number of mailbox placements created (e.g. recipient INBOX + sender Sent).

name.description: The field name as it appeared.

result.description: The result keyword as written upstream. Not checked here.

TagDto.description:
A single `name=value` pair, used for DKIM tags and auth-result properties.

A list of pairs rather than a map: order is meaningful in a DKIM signature,
and a duplicate tag must stay visible rather than silently overwrite.

UpdateWorkspaceRequest.description: Request payload to update an existing workspace.

enabled.description: Whether new notifications are enqueued for it.

has_secret.description:
Whether payloads for this endpoint are signed.

A boolean, never the key. The secret is returned exactly once, by the
create response, and is unreadable afterwards: an endpoint listing is
the sort of thing that ends up in a log or a screen share, and a
signing key that appears there has stopped being a signing key.

WorkspaceDto.description: A workspace summary returned by the API.

auth_required.description: Whether this workspace requires authentication for SMTP/IMAP/POP3.

created_at.description: Created timestamp formatted as RFC 3339 UTC.

is_active.description: Whether this workspace is currently active.

message_count.description: Total count of messages currently in this workspace.

size_bytes.description: Size in bytes on disk for this workspace's database and blobs.
